html:
The Kamaiurá are an Indigenous people of the Upper Xingu in Mato Grosso, Brazil, living by the lake of Ipavu inside the Xingu Indigenous Park. They speak a Tupi-Guarani language.

The peoples of the Upper Xingu speak languages from several different families but share one way of life: villages of large oval houses around a central plaza, manioc farming, fishing, and shared ceremonies. The best known is the Kuarup, a festival for the dead in which villages meet for wrestling and trade. Their name is said to mean a raised platform for keeping meat and pots.

They were long at war with the Ikpeng, who were moved into the park in 1967. Since the 1940s the Villas-Bôas brothers and then the park have protected them from settlers, though fires and ranching now surround the park.
